Industry observers note that domenica contro il Frosinone a San Siro, Strahinja Pavlovic è entrato in campo negli ultimi venti minuti al posto di Diawara, ma non è ancora al 10% dopo il problema i reni che lo ha tenuto fuori nell'ultimo mese e per questo, come riporta questa mattina l'edizione odierna della Gazzetta dello Sport, domani si sottoporrà ad ulteriori accertamenti presso la clinica La Madonnina di Milano. L’obiettivo sarà riaverlo al meglio della condizione per la trasferta di lunedì prossimo in casa del Cagliari di Pisacane.

Come raccontato sia da Sky che da DAZN al termine di Milan-Frosinone, nei minuti finale del match, Pavlovic ha accusato dei giramenti di testa. Al triplice fischio il difensore serbo è stato visto andare subito a sedersi in panchina.

Sources indicate that nella giornata di ieri, il Genoa ha comunicato che Lorenzo Colombo, ex attaccante del Milan, ha riportato la lesione del legamento crociato anteriore del ginocchio destro. Su Instagram, l'ex rossonero ha raccontato tutta la sua amarezza e tristezza per il grave infortunio subito che lo terrà fuori per tutto il resto della stagione: "È veramente difficile trovare le parole in un momento come questo. C’è tanta amarezza, inutile nasconderlo. Stare lontano dal campo, dai miei compagni e da quello che amo fare ogni giorno è la cosa che pesa di più.

Recent findings suggest that non ti aspetti mai di dover affrontare qualcosa del genere, e accettarlo non è semplice. Ma ci sono cose che non possiamo controllare, e quello che possiamo scegliere è come affrontarle. So che mi aspetta un periodo difficile, fatto di pazienza, sacrifici e tanto lavoro. Ma so anche quanto amo questo sport e quanto desidero tornare a viverlo ogni giorno. Grazie di cuore a tutti per i messaggi, l’affetto e la vicinanza che mi state dimostrando. Ci vediamo presto".

Un post condiviso da Lorenzo Colombo (@lorenzo.colombo29).

Credo che in Italia siamo abbastanza bravi a piangere, è una partita importante tre punti valgono per noi come per il Napoli, mi aspetto un Napoli come l’ho visto con il Torino. Sources indicate that intervenuto in un video sul suo canale YouTube, Fabrizio Romano ha parlato così dell'arrivo al Milan di Markus Krosche come nuovo Head of Football: "A proposito di conferme, sono arrivate conferme, e direi finalmente, anche dalla Germania di qualcosa che vi raccontiamo da settimane, ossia che Markus Krosche sarà il nuovo Head of Football del Milan. La realtà è che il Milan l'accordo con Krosche ce l'ha da tempo, il Milan ha tutto pronto anche per l'annuncio ufficiale che è atteso a breve. Il Milan non pagherà 5 milioni, ma 4 milioni di euro di indennizzo all'Eintracht dlFrancoforte per liberare Krosche, che ha già detto addio al club tedesco da diverso tempo. Sarà pronto ed operativo già da inizio dicembre per lavorare al mercato invernale con Gerry Cardinale, con Ruben Amorim e con tutto il gruppo di lavoro che si sta occupando del Milan.

Sources indicate that quindi non ci sono stati dubbi mai di nessun tipo. Markus Krosche è pronto a prendere il controllo del mercato rossonero con Gerry Cardinale, che comunque sarà assolutamente presente, protagonista e coinvolto. Dopo la bella vittoria del Milan contro il Frosinone, il patron milanista ha ribadito che se il Milan andrà a competere per qualche giocatore, ci andrà per vincere e non per partecipare. Insomma, si tratta di un altro segnale dell'ambizione del Milan".

Scegli FcInter1908 come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Antonio Cassano, dagli studi di "Viva El Futbol", ha analizzato il pareggio ottenuto dall'Inter sul campo dell'Atalanta: "Il peggior nemico dell'Inter è l'Inter. Decide l'Inter se giocar bene, se giocar male, prende il Como e lo distrugge. L'Inter decide le sorti del campionato: è più forte, più coraggiosa, ha più qualità, più lunghezza della rosa. Sono convinto che l'Inter ha una grandissima distanza sulla Roma, è la più forte in assoluto".

"Spence? Per me è una pippa, faceva panchina al Genoa, al Tottenham giocava e non giocava, poi si è ritrovato a giocare al Mondiale. Non mi piaceva tanto Dumfries, ma era funzionale a tutta fascia, tutta la vita lui. Tutta la vita anche Diouf, che non sto capendo cosa sta succedendo, prima giocava, era titolare fisso, convocato anche da Zidane. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Sources indicate that tra le pagine dell'edizione odierna del Corriere dello Sport, Alberto Polverosi, giornalista, ha analizzato così il pareggio per 4-4 tra Atalanta e Inter: "Avevano vinto tutte le grandi, quelle della zona-Champions, della zona-Coppe bis e perfino le più deludenti come Napoli e Juventus, peraltro segnando una valanga di gol, e tutti gli allenatori felici e contenti. L’Inter invece è saltata via dalla lista dei tre punti e alla fine in questa galleria di facce sorridenti è mancata proprio quella di Chivu, segnata dallo stress di una partita follemente bella soprattutto per l’Atalanta, che l’ha ripresa su rigore in pieno recupero. Quattro a quattro, l’Inter sempre in vantaggio di due gol e alla fine agguantata da una squadra che non ha pensato nemmeno per un istante di averla persa. Così le romane hanno allungato mentre Milan e Como si sono avvicinate, ma più dei riflessi sulla classifica a Chivu deve interessare un altro tipo di riflessi, quelli tardivi della sua difesa. Che ha preso 17 gol in 12 partite, un numero troppo pesante per chi punta allo scudetto.

L’Inter aveva l’ostacolo più complicato in questa giornata se vista dalla parte delle grandi e se non è riuscita a superarlo, come si poteva immaginare dopo la prima mezz’ora, è stato per merito dell’Atalanta quanto per demerito suo. Era entrata col piede giusto in questa partita, come era accaduto prima della sosta col Como, tanto per far capire che il tempo del risveglio dopo le labbrate era alle spalle. Aggressiva nella metà campo della Dea, ha giocato, costruito occasioni e segnato due gol in trenta minuti. Poi sono sopraggiunti i difetti. Il primo: troppo bellini in area bergamasca, un tocco, due, un passaggino, un colpetto, è mancata la stoccata. Il secondo: sul 2-0, prima flessione mentale, gol di Elmas e partita riaperta. Sul 3-1, seconda flessione e rete di De Ketelaere.

Sul 4-2 terza e doppia flessione con la doppietta del belga e il gol su rigore di Kessie. Completata così una serata che non andrà giù all’allenatore. Nel tentativo di riacciuffare il risultato la partita dell’Atalanta era inevitabilmente cambiata, lasciava spazi di cui Thuram si era impossessato con un paio di contropiedi fenomenali e soprattutto decisivi. Ma nemmeno in quei momenti l’Inter è stata davvero padrona. Sembrava esplodere di salute con un centravanti che sta vivendo il suo momento di grazia. Pio Esposito era passato da Chivu a Mancini e da Mancini a Chivu senza alterare il suo prodotto, i gol. Con la tripletta di ieri, fra Inter e Nazionale è arrivato a otto reti in cinque partite. Tocca una palla e la butta dentro. Intorno a lui stava giocando l’Inter dei momenti in cui niente le è vietato.

Industry observers note that fisicamente straripante, tecnicamente di livello superiore (non solo rispetto all’Atalanta) e poi convinta di quanto sta facendo. Mezz’ora. E poi? E poi su e giù, bene davanti, malissimo dietro, senza equilibrio, senza sentirsi certa della sua forza, oscillava da una parte all’altra del campo, in totale confusione quando doveva difendere. I cambi di Chivu non l’hanno aiutata, mentre quelli di Sarri hanno dato all’Atalanta la spinta decisiva per un’impresa. I complimenti, col punto, vanno all’Atalanta che ha messo la partita (dal 30' del primo tempo fino al recupero del secondo) sullo stesso terreno dei nerazzurri, ritmo, velocità, intensità, aggressività, il secondo tempo della Dea è stato da applausi, quello dell’Inter da incubo".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Si apre la terza fase per la gara del 13 dicembre; nella vendita libera una persona può acquistare fino a quattro tagliandi.

In a recent development, la vendita libera dei biglietti per Lazio-Roma inizierà martedì 24 novembre alle 11:00. Secondo quanto riportato da Sslazio, Si tratta della terza fase di vendita per il derby, in programma domenica 13 dicembre alle 12:30, come comunicato dalla S.S. Lazio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that dalle 11:00 del 24 novembre la vendita sarà aperta per tutto lo stadio. Per i posti dell’intera Tribuna Tevere resterà però obbligatorio possedere una fidelity card Eagle Card o Millenovecento. Per procedere online occorrerà inserire il codice della card come coupon; il codice potrà anche essere presentato al momento dell’acquisto.

Ai biglietti acquistati online sarà applicata una commissione di servizio del 3,80%. I possessori di una fidelity card Millenovecento o Eagle che non sono abbonati potranno chiedere, anche acquistando online, che il titolo d’ingresso sia caricato elettronicamente sulla card.

I biglietti ridotti per invalidi civili al 100% e quelli di Tribuna Tevere per persone non deambulanti, in entrambi i casi con accompagnatore, potranno essere acquistati soltanto nei Lazio Style 1900, escluso il punto vendita di Parco Leonardo. Il ridotto Under 16 è riservato ai ragazzi nati dal 1° gennaio 2010.

According to recent reports, chi compra fisicamente un biglietto in un punto vendita deve mostrare un documento d’identità: senza, il titolo di accesso non può essere emesso, secondo il D.L. 8/2/2010 n. 8. Non sono considerate idonee alla vendita le patenti di ultima generazione che non riportano il luogo di residenza.

Nella vendita libera ogni persona può acquistare al massimo quattro biglietti, secondo le disposizioni dell’Osservatorio sulle Manifestazioni Sportive. Per gli altri tre eventuali intestatari è sufficiente presentare anche una copia del documento d’identità. I bambini di quattro anni nati dal 1° gennaio 2022 entrano gratuitamente e senza biglietto, mostrando un documento d’identità o la tessera sanitaria. All’ingresso l’identità sarà controllata per ogni spettatore: il documento è obbligatorio anche per i minorenni.

Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3256 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources.
  • It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.
  • In a recent development, “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

In a recent development, “Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

Recent findings suggest that “I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”.

What a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

To say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

The Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton mentioned after dodging that bullet.

Industry observers note that and although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

Industry observers note that it could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”.

According to recent reports, could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”.

According to recent reports, gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

Recent findings suggest that he seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

It has been revealed that he told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”.

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”.

It has been revealed that alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”.

Sources indicate that here’s what he said immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”.

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY.

It has been revealed that he says: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”.

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

Alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

It has been revealed that he starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Piastri may be in for some bother.

Hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql.

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs.

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

It has been revealed that alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu.

Pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

According to recent reports, monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

According to recent reports, decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2.

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car firm makes sense, despite what I said earlier.

Recent findings suggest that sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC.

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

In a recent development, the Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”.

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M.

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6.

I’m as big a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car tech giant, isn’t there?

🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx.

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI.

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’.

It has been revealed that “Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

According to recent reports, “What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”.

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft.

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM.

The pair are just natural friends.

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT.

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton mentioned yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”.

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

The full list of times from earlier today.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he noted.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”.

Sources indicate that russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

  • Randal Kolo Muani: preso a parametro zero dal Nantes e rivenduto al PSG per 95 milioni Omar Marmoush: preso a parametro zero dal Wolfsburg e rivenduto al Manchester City per 75 milioni Hugo Ekitiké: preso a circa 20 milioni dal PSG e rivenduto al Liverpool per quasi 100 milioni Willian Pacho: preso a circa 13 milioni dal Royal Antwerp e rivenduto al PSG per 40 milioni Nathaniel Brown: preso a circa 3,5-5,5 milioni dal Nürnberg e rivenduto al Bayern Monaco nell’estate 2026 per 50 milioni fissi + 5 milioni di bonus.

Nella giornata di ieri fonti provenienti dalla Germania hanno confermato che l'operazione tra il Milan e Marcus Krosche è in dirittura d'arrivo: raggiunto un accordo di massima. Era tutto predisposto: nelle scorse settimane il dirigente aveva ratificato le dimissioni dal suo ruolo nell'Eintracht, pur rimanendo sotto contratto con il club. Il Francoforte, che in estate si era irrigidito totalmente sulla possibile partenza di Krosche, in queste ultime settimane ha avuto una posizione più morbida a riguardo e ha dato finalmente il via libera dopo aver annunciato il nuovo DS, Joti Chatzialexiou del Norimberga. Il Milan corrisponderà all'Eintracht una cifra vicina ai 4 milioni di euro e sono attesi i comunicati ufficiali, che dovrebbero arrivare in settimana. Gerry Cardinale aveva individuato il tedesco come "capo del calcio" già in estate e ora, dopo un lavoro diplomatico durato mesi, è arrivato finalmente al traguardo.

Il tedesco nei suoi anni all'Eintracht ha dato una forte struttura organizzativa al club e ha vinto anche una storica Europa League nel suo primo anno di responsabile sportivo del club. È stato inoltre molto efficace nell'andare a pescare giocatori di enorme talento, comprandoli a poco per poi rivenderli a tantissimo. Questi i suoi colpi migliori:.

Randal Kolo Muani: preso a parametro zero dal Nantes e rivenduto al PSG per 95 milioni Omar Marmoush: preso a parametro zero dal Wolfsburg e rivenduto al Manchester City per 75 milioni Hugo Ekitiké: preso a circa 20 milioni dal PSG e rivenduto al Liverpool per quasi 100 milioni Willian Pacho: preso a circa 13 milioni dal Royal Antwerp e rivenduto al PSG per 40 milioni Nathaniel Brown: preso a circa 3,5-5,5 milioni dal Nürnberg e rivenduto al Bayern Monaco nell’estate 2026 per 50 milioni fissi + 5 milioni di bonus.

Al Milan avrà una situazione generale differente: all'Eintracht ha comprato spesso per poi rivendere, dovendo muoversi all'interno di una situazione economica ristretta. In rossonero, soprattutto viste le mire ambiziose di Cardinale, salirà di livello, pur dovendo sottostare ovviamente a logiche di bilancio e dovendo tener conto dei paletti del Fair Play Finanziario UEFA.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

L’Inter continua ad avere problemi nel reparto arretrato. L’assenza di un centrale di esperienza come De Vrij o Acerbi si sente e Chivu non ha ancora trovato l’assetto definitivo. In attesa di trovare una soluzione, il club ha iniziato a guardarsi attorno.

“Non è vero che la migliore difesa sia il requisito minimo dello scudetto: l’Inter di Chivu lo ha dimostrato nella scorsa stagione, dominando anzi il campionato con il miglior attacco e concedendo più gol di Como, Roma e Juventus. Però i numeri di oggi cominciano a essere pericolosi: dopo il 4-4 di Bergamo, e la rabbia per una vittoria buttata via, inquietano gli alti e bassi di una squadra capace di grandi partite, vedi le vittorie contro Feyenoord e Como prima della pausa, e di improvvise amnesie, che sono costate care in Champions (Bruges) e anche in Serie A (il derby, oltre all’Atalanta) dove l’Inter ha conquistato 11 punti nel saldo tra rimonte effettuate e subite. Ecco, guardando il lato positivo Chivu è più avanti rispetto alle prime 12 giornate del 2025 perché ha perso tre partite in meno (una contro quattro) e arraffato 4 punti in più. Ma le avvisaglie di un cedimento strutturale, annunciate da periodici scricchiolii del telaio, sono sempre sotto gli occhi dell’allenatore e dei dirigenti, che stanno provando a risolvere i problemi ma per il momento non hanno individuato la soluzione definitiva”, analizza La Gazzetta dello Sport.

It has been revealed that “La questione mentale è sempre in cima al dibattito interno: la cosiddetta sindrome della vittoria, preconizzata in estate dal presidente Marotta, si insinua di tanto in tanto nelle gambe dei giocatori, che hanno smarrito la ferocia agonistica dello scorso anno e tendono a rilassarsi nella comodità del gioco. Contro l’Atalanta, tre volte in vantaggio di due gol, l’Inter ha abbassato le pressioni e l’attenzione, diventando troppo passiva e restituendo speranza a un avversario che sembrava già fuori dal match. Al pareggio hanno contribuito episodi sfavorevoli, come il rimpallo sull’1-2 di Elmas e il rigore casuale provocato da Bastoni per il 4-4 a tempo scaduto. Ma già in altre circostanze le disattenzioni c’erano state e non avevano generato disastri grazie a un legno, un errore, una parata. Quindi il tema è centrale”.

“Centrale, già, come il ruolo di leader della difesa che per un motivo o per un altro non è stato ancora assegnato: Chivu ha finora alternato in mezzo al terzetto Akanji, Bisseck, Stones e Bastoni senza quasi mai ottenere la necessaria stabilità. Proprio la prolungata assenza di Stones, che era stato ingaggiato per migliorare il reparto in termini di esperienza e personalità, ha lasciato un vuoto enorme, che l’evidente involuzione di Akanji ha aggravato: in 16 partite tra Italia ed Europa sono stati incassati 9 gol in più dell’anno scorso. A oggi la società non prevede di tornare sul mercato a gennaio ma ha cominciato a scrutare il panorama delle occasioni. Non si esclude nulla. E in prospettiva dell’estate prossima si prevede un corposo investimento nel settore, magari per un profilo giovane come il laziale Provstgaard”, chiude Gazzetta.

Com'era il rapporto con Berlusconi?

In a recent development, "A Berlusconi piaceva parlare di calcio, gli piaceva dare suggerimenti anche quando l'allenatore era un po' fuori contesto in quel momento, perché lui aveva sempre la mentalità di avere Van Basten centravanti — Pallone d'Oro — e in panchina il sostituto, Papin. Questo me lo ricordo benissimo: lui voleva che giocassimo con due punte e io cercavo di tamponare per mesi (gli attaccanti erano, Kalinie e André Silva). È difficile perché io facevo le formazioni, è difficile sbagliare formazione perché io me le ricordo tutte. Ero tifoso del Milan, quindi il titolare era Van Basten e la riserva era Papin, entrambi Palloni d'Oro. Quindi, gli dicevo, 'Se lei mi compra qualche giocatore così, stia tranquillo che li faccio giocare tutti e due'".

Industry News: Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

📅 05 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4373 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was the definition of a hard-earned point.
  • Sources indicate that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight.
  • In a recent development, even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Sources indicate that newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

In a recent development, even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

According to recent reports, ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

In a recent development, for the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It highlights where we have potential,” he mentioned. “There are elements to improve offensively.

Recent findings suggest that “The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”.

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In a recent development, in truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a latest manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

It has been revealed that when Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

In a recent development, it is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj.

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another latest signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

In a recent development, bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

It has been revealed that speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads indicated the right reaction.”.

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx.

According to recent reports, 3 - Bournemouth are the first team in Premier League history to score the opening goal in their first three games of a season and fail to win any of them (D2 L1).Fragile. pic.twitter.com/8mBbabT0VV.

"Since the newly introduced manager's come in, all the attacking players have had meetings before the game." 👀Jacob Ramsey reveals how Matthias Jaissle is working with Newcastle's attacking players.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/m7lyG29MlE.

It’s all over at St James’ Park. Newcastle come from two goals down to salvage a hard-fought point against Bournemouth. For the third Premier League game running, Rose’s side have dropped points from a winning position by conceding a late goal, while the hosts’ unbeaten start to the season continues. On the balance of play, a draw is a fair reflection. Both sides really gave it everything.

Jacob Ramsey grabs a late equaliser to complete a Newcastle comeback against Bournemouth pic.twitter.com/qb5i4oaBO9.

According to recent reports, dedic takes the free-kick and curls it over the bar from a long way out. Bournemouth make a very late change as Scott is off for Christie.

Sources indicate that smith clatters into Barnes for a late booking. It’s wave after wave of Newcastle pressure at the moment as Barnes wins a free-kick against Cook.

The noise inside St James’ Park is incredible. The home fans are roaring on the Newcastle players to find a third goal. Bournemouth look absolutely exhausted.

Sources indicate that amid the late drama, Bournemouth make another two changes as Gannon-Doak and Jebbison replace Tavernier and Rayan. There will be six minutes of added time. Can either side find a late winner?

In a recent development, bournemouth fail to deal with a looped cross into their penalty area and can’t clear the danger. Barnes’ initial effort is blocked and the ball breaks to Ramsey, who slams a clinical low strike into the bottom corner to send the Newcastle fans wild. The hosts from come from two goals down, but can they go on and win it now?

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4.

Murphy does brilliantly to beat Truffert to the ball and drive down the wing. The Bournemouth defender has a hold of his shirt and is booked.

Scott rolls a short free-kick into Tavernier, who is allowed to carry the ball to the edge of Newcastle’s penalty area. After a few touches, he shoots, but his thunderous effort comfortably flies off target.

It has been revealed that the current state of the game suits Bournemouth. There’s been a lot of fouls from both sides, halting the rhythm. It’s been very stop-start in this second half.

Safe to say that the Newcastle fans are not happy with the referee. Fernandez-Pardo stands on Smith, giving Bournemouth a free-kick. The home support loudly boo the decision.

Newcastle respond with another double substitution. Steur and Murphy are on, with Nico and Elanga departing the action.

The pace of this game has slowed down in the last 15 minutes, with both sides starting to look really tired. Bournemouth then make two changes as Cook and Brooks replace Adams and Kluivert.

Recent findings suggest that jaissle is booked for breaching his technical area while appealing a refereeing decision. Bournemouth are sinking deeper and deeper as they try and hold on to their slender advantage.

Fernandez-Pardo has been tasked with unlocking Bournemouth’s defence in this closely-fought encounter, but is still waiting for his moment.

Kluivert hauls newly introduced signing Fernandez-Pardo and is given a yellow card, prompting cheers from the Newcastle fans.

It looks like Fernandez-Pardo will slot into the No.10 position behind Wissa as Newcastle continue their search for an equaliser. Bournemouth are defending well as a unit in this second half.

Newcastle’s double-change is here as Fernandez-Pardo comes on for his debut, replacing Willock. The other alteration sees Ramsey come on for Miley.

Newcastle have been the more aggressive side since the restart. Hall cuts inside and after receiving a short corner and shoots, but his effort is high and wide. Fernandez-Pardo and Ramsey look like they’re stepping up their respective warm-ups as they prepare to enter the action.

Wissa is booked for unceremoniously barging Adams in an off-the-ball collision. Jaissle can’t believe it and passionately demonstrates his frustration towards the referee and fourth official.

Just like the first half, there’s also been a fast start to the second. Both managers are still pacing up and down their technical areas.

It has been revealed that newcastle are so close to a leveller! Wissa drives forward from inside Newcastle’s half, then dribbles away from Scott, before skipping past Silva. He manufactures some space and clips a pinpoint cross into Willock, who glances a header agonisingly wide of the far post. That was brilliant play from Wissa.

Newcastle get in behind Bournemouth’s backline as Willock latches onto Hall’s through ball. The former Arsenal academy graduate plays in Barnes, whose one-on-one attempt is smothered by Petrovic. The offside flag was then raised against the Newcastle attacker.

In a recent development, we are back under way for the second half. Here we go again.

Three @premierleague games ✅Two @premierleague goals ✅ pic.twitter.com/B46guzqUjm.

A thrilling first half comes to a close. What a fantastic game of football so far. Bournemouth flew into a two-goal lead through Tavernier’s composed finish and Thiaw’s own goal, before Newcastle pulled one back thanks to Barnes’ superb strike. The visitors are in front, but it’s still all to play for at St James’ Park.

Two goals in two minutes leaves it intriguingly poisedIt's Newcastle 1-2 Bournemouth at half-time pic.twitter.com/iqTsAKRuVF.

There will be three minutes of added time to finish off this breathless first half. Can Newcastle find a late leveller before the break or will Bournemouth restore their two-goal advantage?

It’s end-to-end at St James’ Park. This game is being played like a basketball match. Both teams are flying forward in numbers at every opportunity.

Sources indicate that oh dear not a great moment for two of Newcastle’s summer signings as Bournemouth extend their lead. Amar Dedic lost the ball with a heavy touch and Nico Gonzalez’s half hearted tackle failed to halt Bournenouth’s counter attack.

There was misfortune after with the ball spinning into his own net off Malick Thiaw but Newcastle have been abject.

Thankfully for their manager and supporters, Harvey Barnes’ wonder strike, out of nothing, has got them back into a game they have looked second best in every area of the pitch so far.

Industry observers note that what a goal! 27 seconds after the kick-off, Barnes darts inside of Adams and curls an incredible effort into the top corner. Newcastle are back in it and St James’ Park is alive again.

Barnes provides an immediate response for Newcastle, what a hit! 🚀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eIhwkvoMl0.

Industry observers note that st James’ Park cannot believe it. Kluivert tries his luck from range and his whipped effort strikes the post. Scott follows up and attempts to tee up Evanilson with a cross. It takes a wicked deflection off Thiaw and loops over Hornicek for an own-goal. Bournemouth are in dreamland.

Industry observers note that bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39.

Running the risk of sounding like a broken record but Scott is running the show in midfield. Tavernier has also made a very effective start and scored the opener via a brilliantly-taken opener. Truffert has also produced a magnificent, well-rounded display in defence and attack so far.

It has been revealed that newcastle have been very, very poor. Bournemouth have been excellent. As they have tended to be on their trips to St James’ Park.

Newcastle cannot build any cohesion or momentum in the game. They look disjointed and disorganised. Bournemouth have had ten shots compared to Newcastle’s one.

Easily the worst half an hour of Matthias Jaissle’s short time in charge and as bad as anything we have seen from Newcastle in front of their own supporters for a while.

Bournemouth’s high press works again and the ball breaks loose to Kluivert. He shoots from range and his deflected strike flies narrowly wide of the post.

Recent findings suggest that elanga’s frustrating afternoon continues as he collides with Silva as both players compete for the ball. The Newcastle winger picks up the game’s first yellow card because of the challenge.

According to recent reports, the away side storm forward on the counter as Scott finds Truffert with a piercing pass. The Bournemouth left-back exploits the space vacated by Dedic. Truffert picks out Tavernier with a low cross, but the Englishman’s tame effort is saved by Hornicek. You would expect a lot more from Tavernier there, but Bournemouth look so dangerous going forward.

Bournemouth defend a couple of Newcastle corners in quick succession. The hosts are yet to create a notable chance.

It has been revealed that there’s a real intensity to this game. Bournemouth are attempting to match Newcastle’s pace and physicality in every department. Just now, there was a really interesting battle between Willock and Adams, with the Newcastle man eventually winning a free-kick after a strong dribble.

Industry observers note that bournemouth look to have found a rhythm, with Scott dictating proceedings from the centre of the pitch. Truffert has done well early on to deal with Elanga’s attacking threat.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

Sources indicate that the hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under upcoming head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

It has been revealed that despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. Newly introduced signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Industry observers note that marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

Sources indicate that at opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il tennista sarà operato a Turku il 24 novembre; le prime stime indicano un recupero di circa tre-quattro mesi.

In a recent development, jannik Sinner ha deciso di sottoporsi a un intervento al ginocchio destro. L’operazione è programmata per martedì 24 novembre a Turku, in Finlandia, e sarà eseguita dal professor Lasse Lempainen. La scelta arriva dopo diversi consulti medici e oltre quattro mesi di terapie conservative che non hanno dato i risultati sperati.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Le prime stime indicano un recupero di circa tre-quattro mesi. Il rientro potrebbe avvenire in primavera, ma i tempi dipenderanno dall’esito dell’intervento e dalla successiva riabilitazione.

According to recent reports, il 12 luglio Sinner aveva conquistato il suo secondo Wimbledon consecutivo battendo Alexander Zverev in finale. Quella partita è stata anche la sua ultima apparizione ufficiale della stagione. Nelle settimane successive il tennista italiano ha cominciato ad avvertire dolore al ginocchio destro.

Il problema è stato identificato come una sindrome della bandelletta ileotibiale, che provoca dolore nella parte esterna dell’articolazione. Per un atleta sottoposto a sollecitazioni continue può diventare particolarmente fastidiosa.

All’inizio Sinner e il suo gruppo di lavoro avevano scelto di evitare la chirurgia. Il percorso prevedeva riposo, fisioterapia e trattamenti specifici, con l’obiettivo di recuperare gradualmente la piena funzionalità del ginocchio senza correre rischi inutili o compromettere ulteriormente la carriera del tennista.

Nonostante i tentativi e i consulti con diversi specialisti, il dolore non è scomparso definitivamente. Il numero due del mondo ha quindi preso in considerazione l’intervento. Decisivo è stato l’ultimo confronto con Lempainen, chirurgo ortopedico finlandese specializzato nel trattamento delle lesioni muscolari e tendinee degli sportivi professionisti.

It has been revealed that tra gli atleti già seguiti dal medico figurano anche i calciatori Ousmane Dembélé e Leonardo Spinazzola. Dopo la valutazione della situazione clinica di Sinner, la scelta è ricaduta sull’operazione a Turku.

Nell'ultima puntata di Numer1 Podcast, Giuseppe Cruciani si è espresso sul rigore concesso contro l'Inter nel finale della partita di Bergamo contro l'Atalanta. Queste le sue considerazioni:.

"Mi rivolgo a Orsato: ma un difensore, come diavolo deve saltare? Non si può trasformare in una mummia. Cambiamo le regole. Quello di Bastoni non può essere rigore. E' un rigore farlocco, fake. It has been revealed that "Dire ogni volta che l'Inter è presuntuosa o che sbaglia l'approccio lascia il tempo che trova. Oggi tanti fenomeni dicono che Chivu ha sbagliato i cambi, ma se l'Inter avesse vinto 4-3 avrebbero detto che aveva azzeccato i cambi e risparmiato energie per la Champions. Vi dico che la Roma è strafavorita e questa mia tesi ha trovato conferma. Lazio? Sarebbe fantastico ma sono realistico e non credo possa accadere. Il Milan? Dipende anche da quello che farà Cardinale. Io resto dell'idea che la Roma sia favorita per lo scudetto al 60% e il pareggio dell'Inter, a cui do il 40%, me lo conferma. Non do alcuna possibilità al Milan. La Roma è un rullo compressore: davanti ha un fenomeno".

"Quello che è successo a Bergamo smentisce tutti quei cazzoni che sostengono che tutti sarebbero dei burattini nelle mani di Marotta. E' una cazzata spaventosa. La mancata espulsione di Zappacosta e il rigore concesso all'Atalanta smentisce queste voci".

È su questo legame che punta per trattenere i protagonisti della squadra, mentre cominciano a circolare le prime voci di mercato.

Gattuso ha cercato di coinvolgere tutti, dando spazio anche a chi in precedenza si sentiva fuori posto. Il gruppo viene descritto attraverso i sorrisi, le parole e il clima tra i calciatori, ora al primo posto. Ai giocatori è attribuita una presa di posizione collettiva: «Siamo con Rino. Lottiamo per lui».

Recent findings suggest that nel rapporto con la squadra pesano anche la fame maturata dopo Zenica e l’idea di calcio affinata dal tecnico negli anni. Il modello della Lazio come gruppo familiare viene richiamato attraverso la storia del club, a partire dal primo scudetto. Sabato, all’Olimpico, i tifosi hanno cantato il nome di Gattuso.

According to recent reports, da giorni circolano interessamenti per gli olandesi Taylor e Noslin e per i danesi Isaksen e Provstgaard. Isaksen è stato tra i primi a esprimersi pubblicamente sul proprio futuro. Il Brentford di Matthew Benham lo corteggia: l’imprenditore britannico è noto per il lavoro svolto con Brentford e Midtjylland, il club nel quale l’esterno danese è emerso. Benham conosce bene il calcio danese.

Alla prospettiva della Premier League, Isaksen ha risposto: «La Premier? Voglio la Champions con la Lazio». Anche Provstgaard piace da tempo in Inghilterra. Taylor e Noslin possono attirare offerte, mentre Frattesi ha rifiutato alcune opzioni sia a gennaio sia a luglio.

Finora nessuno dei giocatori ha manifestato a Gattuso la volontà di partire. Da Taylor a Noslin, da Isaksen a Frattesi, prevale l’intenzione di proseguire il percorso con la Lazio. Le posizioni espresse dai calciatori chiamano la società a rispettare il patto costruito tra allenatore e squadra.

Breaking: VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

It has been revealed that the significant moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Industry observers note that replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

Industry observers note that on this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams remarked: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”.

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” noted Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”.

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

It has been revealed that the grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

Industry observers note that one of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi stated: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something notable.

It has been revealed that “If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with significant qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”.

In a recent development, after the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

The substantial headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca stated, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just stated he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

Recent findings suggest that “I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very vital that he is with us.”.

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

Industry observers note that we have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

La Juve anche ha avuto contatti per Varela.

Recent findings suggest that L'Inter è andata a vederlo tante volte ma in attacco ad oggi si ritiene al completo coi suoi quattro attaccanti: poi vedremo se valuterà di fare un'eccezione o se lo considererà solo un'opzione estiva. Se arriva un pacchetto da 30-35 milioni si può arrivare a dama già a gennaio. Nell’anticipazione dell’intervista, Francesca Fagnani suggerisce la prima parola della sigla latina.

Francesco Totti è alle prese con gli acronimi SPQR e LGBTQIA+ in un’anticipazione della sua intervista a Belve. L’ex capitano della Roma fatica a ricordare il significato della prima sigla e risponde con alcune battute alle domande di Francesca Fagnani sulla seconda. Lo scambio è riportato da Cinemaserietv.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Tra le prime domande dell’anteprima c’è quella su SPQR, l’acronimo latino che compare da secoli sullo stemma di Roma e che per anni è stato presente anche sulle maglie giallorosse. Totti non sembra ricordarne con precisione il significato: «SPQR erano quelle… che era… ‘na cosa che nun me ricordo bene».

According to recent reports, fagnani gli suggerisce la prima parola, Senatus. L’ex numero dieci prova a proseguire, poi si ferma: «Senatus? Mo’ pure il latino vuoi… Senatus Popolusco e Romanus so’ troppe frasi».

Recent findings suggest that la conduttrice passa quindi a LGBTQIA+. Totti sembra non riconoscere l’acronimo e, inizialmente, lo associa alla tecnologia: «LGBT? Nun so’ tecnologico io. LGBTQ Plus. Ma che è, un telefonino?».

According to recent reports, fagnani insiste con la domanda e l’ex calciatore continua sullo stesso tono ironico: «18 Plus? Ma ndo’ le tiri fuori ‘ste domande?. Ma come famo?». Il botta e risposta fa parte delle anticipazioni dell’intervista che Totti concederà alla conduttrice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dopo le rassicurazioni a Gattuso, il club valuta un ritocco dell’ingaggio: prima affronterà i contratti in scadenza nel 2028.

In a recent development, kenneth Taylor vuole restare alla Lazio a gennaio e il club pensa a un ritocco del suo ingaggio. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, il centrocampista ha rassicurato Gattuso dopo l’interesse arrivato dalla Premier League e dalla Juventus. La società intende occuparsi prima dei contratti in scadenza nel 2028, poi affrontare anche la sua situazione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, durante la sosta della scorsa settimana a Formello, Rino era in allarme per le sirene del mercato. Sono bastate poche parole di Taylor per tranquillizzarlo. Il giocatore gli ha confermato l’interesse ricevuto: «È tutto vero, i miei agenti mi hanno informato.» Gli ha però chiarito che non intende partire a gennaio: «Ma ho già detto che a gennaio non ci penso proprio ad andare via.».

Taylor ha espresso a Gattuso anche il suo obiettivo: «Voglio restare qui e aiutare la Lazio a tornare in Champions». Il tecnico non si aspettava questa risposta e ne è stato molto felice. Isaksen e Provstgaard gli avevano già promesso fedeltà e appartenenza. A 24 anni, Taylor è descritto come un giocatore già affermato, pronto per un salto di livello e capace di trovare posto in molte grandi squadre italiane e non solo.

According to recent reports, anche Fabiani e Lotito vogliono trattenere Taylor. Se il suo percorso proseguirà così, a giugno potrebbero non bastare neppure 40 milioni di euro per convincerli a trattare con Juventus, Brentford e Bournemouth. La Lazio vuole ricompensarlo per l’attaccamento mostrato e per aver rinunciato a guadagni più alti offerti altrove.

Dopo aver affrontato i contratti in scadenza nel 2028, il club parlerà di un possibile adeguamento per Kenneth, che percepisce 1,7 milioni di euro fino al 2030. A febbraio riceverà il secondo premio fedeltà da 190mila euro, dopo aver scelto per la seconda volta di restare in biancoceleste. Acquistato dall’Ajax per meno di 17 milioni di euro, con il club olandese che conserva il 10% su una futura rivendita, Taylor si è rivelato un colpo straordinario per la Lazio.
