£329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4118 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on upcoming players really does take some doing.
  • According to recent reports, “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium.
  • In a recent development, A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on upcoming players really does take some doing.

According to recent reports, “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

In a recent development, A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

Industry observers note that for Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he stated. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

Indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

Spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

Sources indicate that at the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi noted later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

Recent findings suggest that “There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

Spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This latest stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

It has been revealed that some surprised faces then when Moyes stated later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”.

According to recent reports, the game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes said that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”.

Recent findings suggest that in the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

The first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

According to recent reports, de Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He stated that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

In a recent development, speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender stated: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and revealed that mentality again in the second half.

“We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”.

"I feel like we could've taken three points" James Tarkowski speaks after his sides draw with Spurs 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/Wdj3N5hk8l.

"Six hours and we've not scored a goal? It's a DISGRACE" 😬Ashley Young claims that the Spurs players will need to have conversations about their lack of threat going forward ❌ pic.twitter.com/0KNomGEavx.

"Absolutely diabolical" 😬Jamie Redknapp on Spurs not scoring in their first four Premier League games 😳 pic.twitter.com/48Nbxymlev.

Tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

According to recent reports, boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

FULL-TIME: The points are shared between Spurs and Everton at Tottenham Hotspur stadium 🤝 pic.twitter.com/HwPuKI3Ajh.

Recent findings suggest that dewsbury-Hall’s deflected effort flies out for a corner. Everton can’t make the most of the resulting set piece and Tottenham survive.

There will be three minutes of added time. Are we set for late drama at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium?

Pickford makes an error as his poor clearance is intercepted by Maddison. The ball is eventually worked to Bergvall, whose curling effort is parried away by the Everton goalkeeper.

Jordan Pickford gets down well to deny Lucas Bergvall! 🧤 pic.twitter.com/59uoHTqto6.

In a recent development, tosin comes on for his Spurs debut as he replaces Gray. Can anyone be Tottenham’s hero and find a late winner?

Sources indicate that garner is booked after he clatters into Savio. Everton have produced a tough and disciplined defensive perfomance so far.

Spurs are now enjoying a sustained period of possession. They’re waiting to fashion a big chance and end their wait for a top-flight goal in the 2026-27 season.

Sources indicate that de Zerbi makes another change as Maddison enters the action with applause from the Spurs faithful. He replaces Marmoush. It looks like Tel is now operating as a false nine.

It has been revealed that johnson misses a huge chance! Dewsbury-Hall fires a low cross into his path and Johnson takes the chance with a first-time shot, but he slices his effort and it goes over the bar. He’s got to do better from that range inside the penalty area.

That opportunity is Johnson’s last action of the match as he comes off for Hackney. O’Brien is also introduced, replacing Maitland-Niles.

That was the chance. Dewsbury-Hall rolls it into the path of Spurs’ Europa League final winner Brennan Johnson and he skied it. He hasn’t scored since he left Spurs in January for Palace.

"What a chance this was!"Brennan Johnson had the chance to put Everton in front against his former club 😯 pic.twitter.com/fUi7t6hX7t.

Sources indicate that everton look like the far likelier side to break the deadlock. De Zerbi’s changes have done little to affect the game. Marmoush is cutting a very frustrated figure up top for Spurs.

Bergvall finds Savio with a whipped cross. The winger tries to help the ball back into the danger zone, but Pickford reacts quickly and collects possession.

Dewsbury-Hall picks up the game’s first yellow card after catching Tonali with a late sliding challenge.

In a recent development, what is Kinsky doing?! The goalkeeper’s dreadful pass which was intended for Tonali is intercepted by Dewsbury-Hall, who tries to slide a low effort through Kinsky’s legs. The Tottenham man redeems himself with a crucial save to keep the scoreline goalless. The hosts are living so dangerously. Kinsky needs to wake up.

Antonín Kinský redeems himself after Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall fails to take advantage! 😮 pic.twitter.com/nuKZju90Wz.

Moyes responds with a straight swap on the wing as Grealish comes on for George.

In a recent development, enter: Grealish. He is on for Tyrique George. Surprised that Brennan Johnson survived that change. He has struggled to make an impression.

Recent findings suggest that following Spurs’ reshuffle, it looks like Savio will stay out wide on the right, with Tel on the left. Kudus will sit as the central playmaker behind Marmoush, who is now the lone frontman.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

Jack Grealish has long since stopped the warm-up on the touchline and is now just staring at the game in expectation of his introduction.

A couple of chances for Everton. Spurs have survived but they look so vulnerable when Everton turn over possession. Crowd could turn soon. Almost reached the hour-mark on matchday 4 and still no Spurs’ Premier League goal.

The start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. That day, Tottenham allowed Newcastle to seize the initiative and they netted two second-half goals without reply. Everton are gaining confidence as Spurs continue to lack courage or threat. The crowd is getting more and more restless.

Industry observers note that tottenham fail to clear a corner and the ball lands at George’s feet. The Everton winger shoots but his fierce drive is blocked by Bentancur. The whole of Spurs’ bench is warming up. The visitors currently have the momentum and the hosts look nervous.

Everton are looking threatening once again as George attempts to thread a pass through to Johnson on the counter-attack, but Van de Ven is there to clear.

George does brilliantly to escape away from Gray and floats a cross towards the back post. Barry rises highest and his close-range header is blocked by Kinsky. The Tottenham goalkeeper didn’t know much about it, but that’s a massive stop. Undoubtedly the game’s most dangerous moment in front of goal so far.

Spurs’ first shot has arrived! Unfortunately, Fernandes’ tame long-range effort is easily gathered by Pickford. There were some sarcastic cheers from the Tottenham fans as Fernandes took aim. They clearly want more attacking inspiration from their players.

Recent findings suggest that ironic cheers as Spurs have their first shot on target. It has taken them until the start of the second half and it would be hard to say Fernandes stung the palms of Pickford.

We are back under way for the second half. Everton and Spurs are both unchanged at the break. With the anxiety building in the stadium as the game remains goalless, how long will De Zerbi wait before making a change?

An uneventful first half of football comes to a close. In a game lacking rhythm, creativity and attacking spark, nothing separates Tottenham and Everton at the break. Spurs’ search for a first Premier League goal this season continues.

According to recent reports, there will be two added minutes. Everton have a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are standing over it. The former Manchester United and Nottingham Forest midfielder takes it and his effort bounces in front of Kinsky, who pushes it out for a corner.

James Garner free-kick pushed away by Kinsky is the game’s first attempt on target.

There has not been a single attempt on target at 40:27 from either team. Spurs have had the best of it but even so. That’s a poor return.

Sources indicate that another attack fizzles out for Spurs. Substitute Jack Grealish engaging in some badinage with home fans as he warms up. He famously agreed a move to Spurs in 2018, called off at the eleventh hour when Aston Villa were sold to the current ownership.

That is so poor from Fernandes. The summer signing’s overhit corner drifts out for a goal kick. Suddenly, Spurs’ attacking play has fallen quite flat.

In a recent development, pickford does well to intercept Robertson’s inviting low cross. The left back needed Solanke or Marmoush to make a darting near-post run there to give him more options.

Spurs are bossing this game but on the rare occasions Everton escape you do wonder if they might score.

Recent findings suggest that tottenham are roared on by the home support to move the ball a bit quicker going forward. Out of possession, Everton almost revert to a back five, with Garner dropping very deep near to Tarkowski and Branthwaite.

Tonali picks out Gray with a pinpoint pass. Garner is alert to the danger and tracks back to clear, stopping Gray from getting a one-on-one opportunity.

Maitland-Niles does very well to dispossess Tonali in a dangerous area, allowing Barry to tee up Dewsbury-Hall, but his shot is smothered by the Spurs defence. Mykolenko then chips a cross into a box, but it’s tapped behind for a corner by Robertson. Moyes will certainly be encouraged by this side’s resurgence over the last 10 minutes.

There is a break in play here with Gray down and receiving treatment after a collision. He appears to be holding his lower back. The Tottenham man gingerly gets back to his feet and trudges off the pitch.

Gray down for some extended treatment. Richarlison in the stands. Spurs in danger of losing early momentum.

After Spurs’ fast start, Everton have grown into the contest over the last five minutes and are getting on the ball far higher up the pitch.

Garner’s corner is cleared by Spurs, but only as far as Maitland-Niles. In similar range to where he scored that stunning equaliser against Manchester United, the former Arsenal man shoots, but his attempt fizzes well wide.

It has been revealed that spurs are really flowing here. Finding the balls through the lines and real speed when they attack Everton. Significant question is whether they can convert that into goals. Van Hecke and Fernandes both had chances.

It has been revealed that sávio has had a fine start to the game. Mykolenko in for a long afternoon. Spurs have looked dangerous and should be 1-0 up.

Tonali finds Savio with a deep cross, leaving Pickford in no-man’s land. The Brazilian keeps the ball in play and it loops up, just out of Marmoush’s reach.

Robertson floats a teasing delivery into Van Hecke at the back post, but the centre-back directs his half-volley over the bar from close range.

In a recent development, spurs then burst forward again through Savio, who feeds Fernandes. The playmaker’s low drive is heroically blocked by Tarkowski as Everton continue to hold on (just about).

As expected, it’s Tottenham with all the early possession, with Everton sitting very deep and soaking up the early pressure. Marmoush turns Armstrong and wins a free-kick in a dangerous area.

They’re under way in north London, the hosts are in their lily-white and navy kit, with Everton in their grey/dirty green (is that a colour?!) away number.

Recent findings suggest that greetings from N17. It’s a wonderful, warm late summer evening. As expected there is the usual foreboding from the home fans. Two defeats and one draw. The mood will sour further if Spurs do not win today. No Porro or Udogie so Archie Gray, ever adaptable, starts at right-back again.

Recent findings suggest that everton are undefeated with five points from three games. They have a decent 16/17 players but it is the reserves beyond that which everyone is concerned about. Grealish and Dibling on the bench give them two potential game-changers. Spurs’ squad looks very strong on the team-sheet. A full bench of experienced pros and no fillers. On the pitch it has been less convincing.

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

Industry observers note that the Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

Brennan in the building. 💙 pic.twitter.com/94GgAY8c56.

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

In a recent development, “We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” claims Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

“I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’.

“What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

Everton: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Brathwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry.

Subs: Travers, O’Brien, Keane, King, Alcaraz, Graham, Hackney, Dibling, Grealish.

It has been revealed that after scoring that last-minute leveller against Manchester United last time out, Ainsley Maitland-Niles is promoted to the starting 11 and replaces Merlin Rohl. Brennan Johnson returns to his former club and starts, while Jack Grealish is on the bench.

In a recent development, roberto De Zerbi has made four alterations from last weekend’s stalemate with Nottingham Forest. Dominic Solanke, Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray and Andy Robertson all come into the line-up. Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie are out injured, while Conor Gallagher and Mathys Tel are relegated to the bench. Tosin Adarabioyo and James Maddison are also among the substitutes.

Our Spurs side to take on Everton 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/n637s7swiD.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Sources indicate that are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

According to recent reports, this game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

In a recent development, meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.
